question: True or false: US heart-attack patients just past their 80th birthday got bypass surgery less often than those just short of it?
answer: True. Olenski and colleagues compared patients admitted within two weeks either side of turning 80, alike at baseline. About 7% of those still 79 had bypass surgery, against 5.3% of the new 80-year-olds. A few weeks of age changed nothing in their hearts; it changed the first digit on the chart.
move: A threshold in the head is not a threshold in the body.
ask: Which threshold am I treating as real in my head when my body or situation shows none?
trap: Assuming doctors weigh the patient's health, not the digit in front.
